mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain depressed but stable, routine commuter demand stays suppressed and retail trips do not recover. Over the next four weeks this should keep RETAIL_REC at or below its recent level rather than lifting it.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay within 3 points of current levels for the full next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM moves down while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, households are staying local for necessities and substituting away from discretionary shopping trips. That should push RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -10 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +5
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 2 weeks after GROCERY_PHARM drops below -10 while RESIDENTIAL remains above +5.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS above zero captures leisure substitution away from indoor retail and recreates weekend crowding in outdoor venues. That substitution should lower RETAIL_REC over the next month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses from negative to positive and stays above 0 for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week mean after PARKS remains above 0 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT falls sharply faster than WORKPLACES, the mechanism is a mobility shock rather than a pure work-from-home shift. Retail access then weakens and RETAIL_REC should decline over the following week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT declines by more than 5 points week-on-week while WORKPLACES changes by less than 2 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not drop in the next weekly mean after TRANSIT falls more than 5 points and WORKPLACES is nearly unchanged.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently elevated RESIDENTIAL use signals more time spent at home and lower discretionary out-of-home shopping appetite. With no offset from transit recovery, this should keep RETAIL_REC below its recent average over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises for four consecutive weeks while RESIDENTIAL remains above +5 and TRANSIT remains below -25.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicates more commuting and city-center circulation, which should lift incidental shopping and retail visits. The effect should appear within two weeks and raise RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises for two weeks and TRANSIT also rises for two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase within 2 weeks after both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS remain elevated relative to WORKPLACES, leisure time dominates weekday patterns and retail demand shifts toward outdoor activity rather than shopping. That mix should depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays above WORKPLACES for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall below its last-4-week mean after PARKS exceeds WORKPLACES for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC both weaken at the same time, it signals broad demand suppression rather than a category-specific shift. Under that regime, retail-and-recreation should continue lower over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -8 and RETAIL_REC is already below -25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds in the next weekly mean despite GROCERY_PHARM falling below -8 while RETAIL_REC remains below -25.
